title: Hook teardown: the delete test
hook: A hook that stops the scroll can still lose the sale.
caption:
A hook that stops the scroll can still lose the sale.
Its second job is to set up the next shot, and that job is easy to skip.

There is a quick test for it. Delete the first three seconds of your ad and play the rest. If the ad still makes complete sense, nothing after the hook needed it. The hook was decoration.

In your numbers this can show up as a healthy hook rate with a weak hold rate. People stop, then leave.

The fix in the video is small. Write the hook as a question that the second shot has to answer, with the product in the answer.

The example is a made-up ad, drawn as a storyboard. No real brand.

Video below, 43 seconds.

script.setup: Idea: a growth lead whose ads stop the scroll but lose people a few seconds later gets one test that shows why. On-screen title (first frame): 'Good hook. Why do they leave?' Expectation the title sets: one clear reason and something to try today. The script gives the reason in the first ten seconds, then beats it with a test that takes a minute and a fix for the hook itself. The example ad is made up (a protein bar) and drawn as a simple storyboard of panels. No real brand, no real ad, no results.

scenes.visual: Title text over a six-panel storyboard of a made-up protein bar ad. The first panel glows, the others are dim.
scenes.voiceover: Your hook stops people. Then they leave at second five. Here's why.
scenes.on_screen: Good hook. Why do they leave?

scenes.visual: A thumb scrolling a phone feed stops on the first panel.
scenes.voiceover: Most teams think a hook has one job. Stop the scroll.

scenes.visual: An arrow draws from panel one to panel two. Panel two lights up.
scenes.voiceover: It has two. Stop them, and set up the very next shot.

scenes.visual: A short tag list appears beside the storyboard: hook, pacing, cast, call to action. The word hook is circled.
scenes.voiceover: We tag the hook on its own, on every ad we decode. So here's one test.

scenes.visual: Panel one is crossed out and slides away. The remaining five panels play in order.
scenes.voiceover: Delete the first three seconds. Play the rest. Does the ad still make sense?

scenes.visual: The five panels sit complete without the first. The removed panel greys out at the side.
scenes.voiceover: If yes, your hook was decoration. Nothing after it needed it.

scenes.visual: The greyed panel is wiped clean and a question mark is drawn on it.
scenes.voiceover: That only finds the gap. To close it, write the hook as a question.
scenes.on_screen: Write the hook as a question

scenes.visual: New panel one: a person at a desk, clock at four, text of the question. New panel two: the bar being unwrapped at the same desk.
scenes.voiceover: 'Why am I hungry by four?' Then shot two answers it, with the product.

scenes.visual: Panels one and two join with a line. Galvor logo end card.
scenes.voiceover: A hook is a promise. The next shot pays it. Follow Galvor for more.

script.music: No music, or a very low instrumental bed under the voice.
script.notes: Native LinkedIn upload, vertical, under 60 seconds. Burn in subtitles. Use the cover slide as the thumbnail. Numbers used: none. The storyboard is a drawn, made-up ad, so no real brand appears. About 100 spoken words.

slides.headline: Good hook. *Why do they leave?*
slides.sub: One test for the first three seconds.
